Let \(b=AB\) and \(d=DE\). Place coordinates so that

\[
A=(0,0),\qquad E=(20,0).
\]

Reflect if necessary so that \(B,C,D\) lie in the upper half-plane. Then

\[
B=(0,b),\qquad D=(20,d),
\]

with \(b,d>0\).

---

### 1. Use the angle at \(B\)

The ray \(BA\) points straight downward. Since \(\angle B=45^\circ\) and

\[
BC=14\sqrt2,
\]

the vector \(BC\) must make a \(45^\circ\) angle with the downward vertical. Thus its vertical drop from \(B\) to \(C\) is

\[
14\sqrt2\cos45^\circ=14,
\]

and its horizontal displacement has magnitude also \(14\). So if \(C=(x,y)\),

\[
y=b-14,\qquad x=\pm 14.
\]

Because \(C\) is on the same side of \(AE\) as \(B,D\), we need \(y>0\), so

\[
b>14.
\]

---

### 2. Use the angle at \(D\)

At \(D\), the ray \(DE\) points straight downward, and \(\angle D=45^\circ\). Therefore the vector \(DC\) must also make a \(45^\circ\) angle with the downward vertical, so its horizontal and vertical changes have equal magnitude.

Thus

\[
d-y=|20-x|.
\]

Substitute \(y=b-14\):

\[
d=b-14+|20-x|.
\]

Now consider the two possible values of \(x\).

- If \(x=14\), then

\[
d=b-14+6=b-8.
\]

- If \(x=-14\), then

\[
d=b-14+34=b+20.
\]

But the problem states \(DE<AB\), i.e. \(d<b\). The case \(x=-14\) gives \(d=b+20>b\), so it is impossible.

Therefore

\[
C=(14,b-14),\qquad D=(20,b-8).
\]

---

### 3. Compute the area

Use the shoelace formula on

\[
A=(0,0),\ B=(0,b),\ C=(14,b-14),\ D=(20,b-8),\ E=(20,0).
\]

The signed double area is

\[
\begin{aligned}
&0\cdot b+0(b-14)+14(b-8)+20\cdot0+20\cdot0\\
&\quad-\bigl(0\cdot0+b\cdot14+(b-14)20+(b-8)20+0\cdot0\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]

This simplifies to

\[
328-40b.
\]

Since \(b>14\), the absolute value gives the area

\[
K=\frac{40b-328}{2}=20b-164.
\]

---

### 4. Impose the divisibility condition

We need the area to be an integer multiple of \(16\):

\[
20b-164\equiv 0\pmod{16}.
\]

Since

\[
20\equiv 4\pmod{16},\qquad 164\equiv 4\pmod{16},
\]

we get

\[
4b-4\equiv 0\pmod{16},
\]

so

\[
4(b-1)\equiv 0\pmod{16}.
\]

Thus

\[
b\equiv 1\pmod{4}.
\]

Also,

\[
b>14,\qquad b<2026.
\]

So the possible integer values of \(AB=b\) are

\[
17,21,25,\dots,2025.
\]

This is an arithmetic progression with first term \(17\), last term \(2025\), and common difference \(4\). The number of terms is

\[
\frac{2025-17}{4}+1=\frac{2008}{4}+1=502+1=503.
\]
